title: From Gin's Book. What Nobody Says Out Loud

blocks.p: The baker's barley tea was still sour in Rei's mouth when he got home. He turned to Chapter Two, because it came next. The preface was dated A Friday. Rain. Rei forgot his umbrella again. Left mine by the door for him. Rei remembered the umbrella. He had not known it was Gin's. He read the chapter at the kitchen table with both lamps on, and twice he got up to check the lock, and both times it was locked.

doc.title: Personal Archive. Chapter Two, preface
lines: What follows is what I know after six years of field work, two years of archive access I was not supposed to have, and approximately four hundred conversations with people who told me things they wouldn't have told me if they had known I was writing them down.

The official framework presented in Chapter 1 is accurate in its facts. It is dishonest in its framing. The Veil is real. Practitioners are registered. The Division manages the boundary. What it omits is the question every new practitioner eventually asks and never gets a direct answer to: managed for whose benefit?
This chapter will make you angry. Let the anger make you careful rather than reckless. Reckless anger gets people killed. Careful anger builds things.
Keys on the hook. Coffee finished. Rei took the umbrella. Good.

doc.title: Psychic Class Structure. Internal CVD Sociological Assessment (Restricted). Level 4+ Clearance
lines: Class One. Tower Families. Generational psychic bloodlines with economic resources to match. Children are assessed at 16, trained privately before registration, and enter the system already equipped and connected. They set the standards everyone else is measured against.

Class Two. Institutional Practitioners. Middle-class or upwardly mobile individuals identified through standard channels. Registered, trained through CVD programs, employed in civil roles. The backbone of the official system. Given enough to make loyalty rational.

Class Three. Unregistered / The Grid. Practitioners who fell through identification channels, refused registration, or actively avoid the system. Disproportionately from lower economic strata, immigrant communities, and marginalized populations. Higher per-capita ability levels than the registered population, per suppressed internal studies.

Class Zero. Protocol Targets. Practitioners assessed as Arbiter rank or above (Level 5+ in CVD classification) who are unregistered or uncontrolled. Not a class in the social sense. The primary focus of the Veil Protocol division's active mandate.

doc.title: Post-it, red ink
lines: The suppressed studies referenced above are real. I have copies.

Trauma and desperation thin the veil faster than comfort and training. The people the system was designed to manage are more powerful than the system knows. It is not about order. It is about the math.

blocks.p: Folded into the page was a cheap photocopied flyer, soft from being carried in a pocket. It had no letterhead. At the bottom someone had stamped Other Side Distribution in blurred purple ink, which Rei would learn later was how the Grid signed things.

doc.title: What They Tell You When You Register (and What They Don't)
lines: They will tell you: registration protects you. And it does. Registered practitioners have legal standing. Unregistered ones have whatever they can argue in the moment.

They will tell you: registration gives you access to resources. Also true. CVD training programs are genuinely good. The equipment they issue to Level 3+ field operatives is better than most of what circulates on the Grid's black market. The salary is stable.

They will not tell you: your file is accessible to seventeen agencies. Your threat assessment, a number generated by an algorithm they will not explain, follows you permanently and can be updated without your knowledge. Above Arbiter rank, the recruitment offer and the compulsory conscription offer look very similar.
They will not tell you about the Protocol's active operations list. Being on it is not a consequence of wrongdoing. It is a consequence of being interesting at the wrong level.
The Grid does not tell you to refuse registration. What the Grid tells you is: know what you are agreeing to. Then make the choice that keeps you alive and functional.

doc.title: Gin's post-it on the flyer
lines: If you're reading this and you're a 5 or above, assume you're already on it. Act accordingly.
I am registered. I chose this. Registration is a tool like any other tool, useful when you control it, dangerous when it controls you. Know which situation you are in.

blocks.p: The next document had a different stamp, darker and heavier, and Gin had not written a caption under it. Veil Protocol Division. Classified Reference. Level 5+ Clearance Required. Top Secret. Protocol Eyes Only. Rei had never heard of a Veil Protocol division. Reading the first paragraph, he understood that this was the point. It was a separate operation that lived inside the Division like a second skeleton. Gin had written one line above the stamp, small. I work for the sixty percent officially. I know about the forty percent because six years of field work teaches you to read what is not written in the operational briefings.

doc.title: The Veil Protocol. Actual Mandate. Classified Mandate Components
lines: Component One. Catalogue. Identification and detailed profiling of all practitioners at Level 3 and above, registered or unregistered. The registered database is the foundation. Unregistered practitioners are identified through field surveillance, informant networks, entity interaction monitoring, and algorithmic flagging of veil activity patterns.

Component Two. Weaponize. Development of military and intelligence applications for psychic ability. Ability amplification, forced ability development, entity recruitment and control, veil manipulation at scale. Conducted at facilities that do not appear on public CVD organizational charts. Staffed by practitioners whose registration files list them as retired, deceased, or transferred to administrative roles.

Component Three. Control. Neutralization of practitioners assessed as uncontrollable variables. Coercive recruitment (offer followed by compulsion if refused), indefinite detention under veil security protocols, ability suppression through pharmaceutical and procedural means, and, in cases assessed as extreme risk, termination. The threshold for extreme risk is not public. It is not consistent. It has been applied to practitioners whose primary offense was refusing recruitment.

doc.title: Gin's margin, urgent
lines: The Component Three threshold document, the internal guidelines for what constitutes extreme risk, I have also obtained. It is in a separate file. If you are reading this archive and I am not available: the file is at the location described in the note on page 147. Do not access it through any networked device.
I was offered registration twice before I accepted. The first offer was polite. The second offer was not.

doc.title: The Towers and Component Three
lines: The Tower families are aware of the Protocol's full mandate and have negotiated their position within it. Their members are not subject to Component Three. They provide practitioners to Protocol research programs voluntarily, and in exchange their bloodlines are classified as protected assets rather than potential threats.

Translation: the old money families agreed to cooperate with the government's psychic weapons program in exchange for their children being marked safe. Everyone else's children are not marked safe. This is the arrangement. It has been the arrangement for forty years. The people who benefit from it call it stability. The people who don't call it something else.

blocks.p: Rei read that page three times. He thought of Sei, alone at seventeen in a house whose children were marked safe, and of Itsuki, who had run from that house to paint bridges. He thought of himself, nineteen, never assessed, in a flat that belonged to no family anyone had heard of. Nobody had marked him anything. He had always taken that to mean nobody had noticed him. It occurred to him for the first time that Gin might have worked very hard to keep it that way.

doc.title: Chapter Two. Closing Note
lines: Same day. Later. Rei's light is off. First time before midnight in a week.

A practitioner I worked a case with in Koenji, Level 4, registered, twenty-four, asked me once why I stayed in the system if I knew what I knew. She had just seen the inside of a Protocol facility for the first time.

I told her: because the work is real. The entity in the Nerima apartment that I didn't disperse because the old woman needed him there, he was real, and his wife was real, and that mattered regardless of what the system around it was doing.
I also told her: the system is a tool. Tools do not have loyalty. Do not give yours to a tool.
Keys were on the hook. Didn't check, just knew. That's new.

blocks.p: Rei closed the book on his finger and sat with the last line. Didn't check, just knew. It sounded like a man getting better at something. Reading it now, at the empty hook, it sounded like a man who had stopped looking.
